about: The floors the evaluation runs alert on (decisions 0126 and 0133). Retrieval floors are per question set and per order: reranked is the order answers read (the fused candidates reordered by the reranker, a restatement folded into a hit counting as that hit), fused is the first-stage order a failed rerank keeps; a null or missing floor is measured and reported but never alerts, and the reranked floors of a set are not compared when any of its questions kept the fused order because the rerank failed. handWritten is retrieval_questions.json, scored by the weekly run and the release check. generated is the whole of generated/retrieval_questions.json (169 questions on 2026-11-22: 58 English and 111 in other languages), scored by the weekly run, whose judge may only widen what counts as found. releaseSample is what the release check scores instead: at most two English questions per craft of that file (41 on 2026-11-22), so it holds only the paraphrased English questions the fused order finds worst, and its fused floors sit far below the whole set's. Set on 2026-11-22 at the live numbers of release db09b9e7 less 0.05, rounded down to two places: handWritten reranked 0.987 and 0.982, fused 0.936 and 0.707; generated reranked 0.994 and 0.917 (the English 1.000 and 0.855 and the other languages 0.991 and 0.950, weighted by their counts), fused 0.787 and 0.700; releaseSample reranked 1.000 and 0.855 (the reranked figures of all 58 English questions, since the sample's own were not measured apart; its fused 0.439 and 0.297 match the 58's 0.414 and 0.296 closely), fused 0.439 and 0.297. Answer floors compare answer-quality's judge and rubric means; they were re-based on 2026-11-22 to the judge that now judges: the first baseline (judge 0.936, rubric 0.911 on 2026-11-21) was judged entirely by Gemini 4 Argon, while answer-quality run 44994632550 on release db09b9e7 (13 answers before its cap) was judged throughout by Claude Opus 5.5, a stricter judge, at a judge mean of 0.815, and its rubric mean rose with round 7's fixes to 0.969; each less 0.05, rounded down. The rubric floor was re-based again on 2026-11-22 when the rubric began to count each sentence a block shows once, as the judge reads it (decision 0147): the lowest rubric mean that count can give on the answers of run 44994632550 is 0.872, since a consulted field keeps at least one sentence and only a field with a figure loses copies; less 0.05, rounded down. The lead raises the floors as the numbers improve. The fused floors were raised on 2026-11-23 when eval_retrieval --fusion on release 1ab422fe picked the weighting k 20, lexical 0.5, vector 5, entity 0.25 (backend/app/data/eval/fusion.json): handWritten fused 1.000 and 0.932, generated fused 0.975 and 0.870 (the 54 English 0.963 and 0.752 and the 103 other 0.981 and 0.931, weighted by their counts), releaseSample fused 0.974 and 0.784; each less 0.05, rounded down. The generated set was written again on 2026-11-23 (eval-questions run 45112560382: 262 questions, 142 in English, keptShare 0.1516 against about 0.08 before) and scored on release 1ab422fe's knowledge with that weighting: generated fused 0.969 and 0.839 (the 142 English 0.951 and 0.751 and the 120 other 0.992 and 0.944, weighted by their counts), releaseSample (61 questions) fused 0.951 and 0.777 and reranked 1.000 and 0.910; the generated fused and releaseSample floors were re-based to those numbers less 0.05, rounded down.
